extracted.intended_audience: researchers (7-12 years post-PhD) preparing and submitting ERC Consolidator Grant applications; host institutions and research administrators supporting applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and rules for researchers preparing, submitting and being evaluated for the ERC Consolidator Grant (eligibility, host institution requirements, application content/submission, funding, ethics review and evaluation process). Targets applicants wishing to consolidate independence by creating/strengthening a research team in Europe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: career stage and dossier
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers of any nationality with 7-12 years of experience since completion of PhD, a scientific track record showing great promise and an excellent research proposal can apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the basic eligibility window for Consolidator Grants; applicants must demonstrate both the required post-PhD time window and a promising scientific track record together with an excellent research proposal. See the ERC Work Programme for details and allowed extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of eligibility (interruptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility can be extended for reasons such as maternity, paternity, or parental leave, illness, national service, clinical training, natural disasters, asylum, or for victims of gender-based violence or any other form of violence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who have had career interruptions for the listed reasons may request extension of the eligibility window. Check the Parental leave webpage and the latest ERC Work Programme for the specific rules and documentation required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference date for eligibility: PhD defence date
rubrics_metrics.description: From 2023, the European Research Council (ERC) changed the reference date for calculating the eligibility window for the Starting and Consolidator Grants. Instead of the date of the actual award, the certified date of the successful PhD defence will be used as a reference point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures fair competition across countries where 'award' dates vary. For applicants where no defence/viva was organised in the awarding institution, the applicant should provide a written confirmation from that awarding institution stating that no defence/viva was organised and indicating the date when the PhD was approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research field openness ('bottom‑up' principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications can be made in any field of research. The ERC's grants operate on a 'bottom-up' basis without predetermined priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are yearly calls covering all scientific fields; no thematic priorities are imposed — evaluation focuses on excellence regardless of field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location requirement / Host Institution (HI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research must be conducted in a public or private research organisation (known as a Host Institution/HI). It could be the HI where the applicant already works, or any other HI located in one of the EU Member States or associated countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The HI must be located in an EU Member State or an associated country. Use of the Host Institution implies institutional commitment and that the HI can provide the necessary environment and infrastructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host Institution responsibilities and commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: The host institution must offer suitable conditions for the PI to independently lead the research and manage funding. The PI can be hosted by any legal entity in an EU Member State or associated country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PI does not need to be employed by the host institution at the time of proposal submission, but a mutual agreement and commitment are necessary if the proposal is successful. The HI must demonstrate it will allow the PI to lead the project independently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single Principal Investigator requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for an ERC grant require a single Principal Investigator (PI) to submit the application on behalf of their host institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Consolidator Grant is a single-PI scheme; consortia or multiple PIs are not permitted for the ERC grant application submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team composition and mobility of team members
rubrics_metrics.description: ERC grants support projects carried out by an individual researcher who can employ researchers of any nationality as team members. It is also possible to have one or more team members located in a non-European country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may recruit international team members and may host non-European scientists through initiatives ('Implementing Arrangements'). Vacancies can be advertised through Euraxess-Jobs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application completeness and required documents
rubrics_metrics.description: For an ERC grant application to be complete, it needs to include the administrative forms, the research proposal and the supplementary documents. The completed proposal needs to be submitted by the specified closing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls are published on this page, the EU Funding & Tenders Portal and in the Official Journal. Ensure all parts (administrative forms/Part A, research proposal/Part B, and supplementary documents including Ethics Issues Table and Ethics Self-Assessment) are included before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission process and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: ERC grant applications can only be submitted in response to a Call for Proposals. The completed proposal needs to be submitted by the specified closing date. You can update your submitted proposal any time before the deadline by simply submitting a new version, which will overwrite the old one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarise yourself with the EU submission service (the online system). Submit as early as possible; deadlines cannot be changed under any circumstances. You will get an ‘acknowledgement of receipt’ by e-mail for each submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding amounts, duration and additional funding rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Consolidator Grants may be awarded up to €2 million for a period of 5 years (pro rata for projects of shorter duration). However, an additional €1 million can be made available to cover further eligible costs when these are necessary to carry out the proposed work. For Principal Investigators currently based in non-associated third countries re-locating to the EU or an Associated Country to take up their ERC grant, the maximum additional funding may be up to €2 million.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for additional funding must be duly justified in the proposal (e.g. start-up costs, major equipment, access to large facilities, major experimental and field work costs). An ERC grant can cover up to 100% of the total eligible direct costs of the research plus a contribution of 25% of the total eligible costs towards indirect costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics review requirement and basis
rubrics_metrics.description: If your proposal is selected for funding it will undergo an ethics review. This is a legal requirement under the Horizon Europe Framework Programme - Regulation 2021/695: Eligible actions and ethical principles (Article 18) and Ethics (Article 19). The basis for this ethics review is Part A (including the Ethics Issues Table – EIT – and the Ethics Self-Assessment – ESA) and Part B of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A well-detailed Ethics Self-Assessment (ESA) is crucial to facilitate the process as it clarifies what issues are linked to the proposed research activities and how these will be dealt with. Certain topics (e.g. research involving hESCs) require additional specific EC approval following programme committee procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics review stages and applicant responses
rubrics_metrics.description: The ethics review comprises 3 stages: Ethics pre-screening (performed internally by ERCEA staff), Ethics screening (panels of Independent ethics reviewers identify proposals with potentially Serious and/or Complex ethics issues), and Ethics assessment (panels of independent ethics reviewers discuss Serious and/or Complex ethics issues).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-screening clears proposals without ethics issues or with simple ethics issues. Clearance of proposals with non-Serious and/or Complex ethics issues can include observations and references to documents to be kept on file and provided to ERCEA upon request. After screening, applicants might be contacted (typically one week after the screening panel) and are given 3 weeks to reply with additional information. For serious/complex issues, ethics deliverables might be required during project implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation principle: excellence as sole criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are evaluated by selected international peer reviewers who assess them on the basis of excellence as the sole criterion. It will be applied to the evaluation of both the research project and the Principal Investigator in conjunction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both the project's scientific excellence and the PI's excellence are considered together. There are no other award criteria beyond excellence for ERC grants; reviewers score and assess accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review process, scoring, quality threshold and ranking
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers are in charge of assessing and scoring the proposals. Those who pass the quality threshold are ranked. Depending on the call budget available, a budgetary cut-off applies to the ranking list and only the highest ranked proposals are offered an ERC grant until the call's budget has been used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation relies on both panel members and external referees. Passing the quality threshold is necessary to be placed on the ranked list; final selection is by ranking within the available budget (budgetary cut-off).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation panels and role of remote referees
rubrics_metrics.description: For each call there are 28 panels, each covering a sub-section of one of three domains: Life Sciences (LS), Physical and Engineering Sciences (PE) and Social Sciences and Humanities (SH). Each ERC panel consists of a chair and 10-16 members. In addition to the panel members (who act as “generalists”), the ERC evaluations rely on input from remote experts external to the panel, called referees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel chairs are published before the deadline; full panel membership is published after evaluation concludes. Panels combine generalist panel members and specialised remote referees to ensure appropriate expertise for evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application preparation best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the call is published: find out which ERC grant and which call is suitable; identify the Host Institution and team members; contact the National Contact Point (NCP). Once the call is open: read the call documents carefully; contact the Host Institution and gather all details; start writing your proposal and allow time for others to review; familiarise yourself with the EU submission service; submit early and update before the deadline if needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Get support and feedback from NCPs, peers and other scientists; use online research partner search services if needed; submit early because deadlines cannot be changed; you will receive an acknowledgement of receipt for each submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special ethics/legal approval for human embryonic stem cells (hESC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research proposals involving the use of hESCs will need to undergo all of the steps of the Ethics review and also a specific EC approval following a consultation to the HE programme committee comitology procedure, as this is a legal requirement under HE framework programme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for extended ethics scrutiny and additional approval processes for hESC-related research; ensure the ESA and EIT fully document and justify the work and compliance.
